name: Immunex-TiBio
description: Immunex-TiBio is a commercially pure titanium substrate that undergoes a proprietary BioForge surface-treatment process in which the outer 40-80 nanometers of the metal are replaced with a molecularly bonded layer of host-matched glycoprotein analogs — synthetic versions of the cell-surface proteins that tell the immune system 'this is self.' The result is a titanium implant that the host's immune system registers as native tissue, eliminating rejection responses, chronic inflammation, and the immunosuppressant regimens that previously defined augment aftercare. Each batch is genetically customized to the recipient.
cost: Φ9,000–Φ28,000 per implant unit (price varies by complexity and recipient genotype mapping)
story_hooks: BioForge's Immunex-TiBio genetic customization database contains the complete immune profiles of every recipient — a data breach exposes not just identities but the biological vulnerabilities of hundreds of thousands of augmented individuals.

A counterfeit Immunex-TiBio operation is selling uncustomized generic-formula implants as personalized units — recipients don't reject them immediately, but a slow-burn autoimmune cascade is building in thousands of patients who won't understand the cause for years.

A forensic investigator discovers that a murder victim's Immunex-TiBio implants were customized to someone else's immune profile — meaning the victim received an implant intended for another person, suggesting a deliberate identity-concealment operation.
